To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) significant differences exist in students’ percentages of mobile phone use, students’ dependence of using mobile phone, and the number of schools that banned students’ mobile phone among elementary, middle and senior high schools; (2) significant differences exist between schools in the oral and written forms of banning mobile phone use and in policy enforcement; (3) no school-level difference was found in students’ fondness for mobile phone use, in teachers’ assessments of the effectiveness of the mobile phone policy, and
there are significant differences in mobile phone use and policy at elementary, middle schools, and high schools.
there were significant differences in mobile phone policy implementation among schools of different levels, and that the differences were mainly in the policy enforcement strategies.

, in the context of Chinese elementary, middle, high schools, mobile phone policies should be more effective if (a) they are reinforced by teachers and parents, (b) they are implemented in a consistent manner, and (c) they are enforced in a timely manner.
mobile phone policies are not the same in elementary, middle, or high schools, but they should be.

schools should be aware that mobile phones can be used as a distraction to the learning environment and can also be a source of anxiety.

, in order to effectively manage students’ mobile phone behaviors in school, schools should take into account differences in students’ mobile phone usage and dependence, and develop mobile phone policies that are appropriate for different school levels.
